author: Zintenka
body:
Give MapDevs Kick
Because when a MapDev wants to test a map they need to be able to kick anyone who is disrupting the test like a hacker or a really rude person. And sometimes, moderators aren't online or are handling other reports.

This would not only moderators' jobs easier but will make map testing more convenient for MapDevs.

Stop Banning People For Wanting To Give IPs For Build Servers, UHCs Or Anything That Falls Within
It's petty to ban someone who wants the IP for a build server such as Alex's or something else. Like, this genuinely doesn't make any sense whatsoever.

I see someone who posts an IP for a build server years ago and a mod comes to the post and warns them that they'll be banned if they do this again. I'm like: "Woah. Bruh, chill. It's only for a build server, holy shit."

It's impractical to ban someone for this. Damn.

Make It A Requirement For Staff Members To Be on Community Slack
It's inconvenient for players if they need staff members to come online or to ask a question and they don't even respond because 90% of the time they're offline.

It's not that hard to check in with community slack once in awhile staff, just have it open in one of your TABs. And if you see a red circle by the Slack TAB icon then you'll know when you're needed. Like seriously, c'mon.

Developers shouldn't be exempt from this rule, players and mapmakers especially have a lot of questions for them and I haven't even been able to get into contact with even one since being on Community Slack...

Stop Participating in Censorship in Staff Team
I've heard from many former moderators that they aren't allowed to openly criticize the staff team or else they'll be demoted. This is absolutely ridiculous.

Criticism allows people to see what is wrong with themselves and work to improve themselves. The same applies for an institution, stop turning the staff team into a high-level corporation. 

Don't be like that PMC (Private Military Corporation) who fired anyone in MSNBC who disagreed with the Iraq War. This is disgusting and makes me want to reconsider applying for mod. It should make anyone here reconsider.

However, the demotion for Leaks should be left alone. Sensitive information is sensitive, and I understand this.

Perhaps Move the Staff Applications Period By a Month?
A lot of people in here are going to College, anyone who lives in America will go to college THIS MONTH on the 26th. Maybe.

There's a lot that needs to be done to make sure that everyone has their shit properly set up. A staff application would've been great in June or July but you moved it to the month that people are going to college because of... what?

The best thing possible is if applications are done in September after everyone has settled in.

replies.author: OldManTigerMask
replies.body:
Never got in contact with any staff on slack since I've joined. Oh please I've only joined about a week ago and talked to 3 - 5 staff frequently, some of the miss that reply often are, Jahaj, Junr and Cammy. They're very nice and easy to talk too.

Although I cannot disagree that staff do need to be active on slack and on the forums.

Move staff apps?

Not really, August is a great time for other timezones and is beneficial to many, even if the format has not been posted, we all have a fairly good idea what they're gonna ask, so we can prepare, and you still have 15+ days till colleague so I'm pretty sure it's fine.

Banning IP address revealing, Yes I agree that it shouldn't be changed but I also would think staff should allow flexibility in private messages. I think it should depend on the circumstance, for example if a dude says Join my server /msg me, of course you can ban him. But if the dude is like telling a friend, hey can you please join my servEr? Ip is this.is.myip.com.

okay I agree with most of the points though and nothing personal, 
thanks,
Tiger

replies.author: Zintenka
replies.body:
1 - Give me one?
3 - Community Slack is still an Avicus platform. How is it external? Players need to ask staff members questions because they are STAFF MEMBERS.

It prevents topics that border on spam such as this one https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/e11fb7d05

This could've been easily given out by a MapDev or a Developer. I needed it for me and Junr's map: "Juntenka". XML filters is a really complicated process to do, make certain blocks indestructible to different causes and how to position this and that...

I got the answer 7 hours after asking and I had to go on Teamspeak. A MapDev was conveniently there. But if they weren't I probably would've waited several more hours or never get an actual direct answer.

Then "Juntenka" would've been a broken, incomplete map. Having this rule would actually improve staff - player relations.

5 - Oh, yeah I see what you mean by this. Forgot about different regions and stuff xD

replies.author: Zintenka
replies.body:
@Para
Yes! This! Developers, make it happen!

@OldManTigerMask
You sort of exaggerated my point on the staff slack part. I said 90% of the staff, doesn't mean not a single one. I also talk with Junr and others quite often but the others...? Not so much.

And I made the "Not a single one" comment in regards to Developers because we Map makers need to know what we're doing when we're coding XML for our maps. It would be really inconvenient to mess up in Atlas' XML considering that we don't have a viable platform to test Atlas maps on.

And it will likely take a few weeks to test a map just to solve One or two single lines of code.

This is impractical for us.

I understand that August is a good time for many timezones, I'll drop this issue now xD

Build servers don't really pose a threat for Avicus' population. In fact, it's a boon because these build servers are posting to allow players to make maps for Avicus!

There was never anything personal my friend ;)

@Junr
True, but it would allow for people to have multiple build servers to chose from in case Alex's shuts down or they're banned from it for being a douche :P

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
I've heard from many former moderators that they aren't allowed to openly criticize the staff team or else they'll be demoted.

This isn't a staff problem, I feel like it could be more of a confidence problem with those specific staff members.

 When I was a Mod, I criticised the staff team and the seniors all the time.
And because I was just giving my opinion, I obviously wasn't demoted for it.

Moderators just need to be confident. 
They assume that they'll get demoted, but they won't.
If you voice your opinion, even if it's a minority view, you will not get demoted.

This has never been the case in the staff team and never will be.

And tbh if it actually was, I'll have a long talk with Posighdun about it.

But because I know Sessp's abilities in the staff team, I know for a fact that he would never let this happen.

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
MapDevs being able to kick people isn't a good idea.
This could lead to abuse and a lack of training for some could lead to unjust and incorrect kicks.

Staff being active on the community slack would be very nice but shouldn't be a requirement.
In the same way that community members shouldn't be 100% active on the community slack. 

The apps being around this time works perfectly for me personally.

I do agree with you about the whole ip thing.
Moderators do need to be fully aware of the situation before permanently banning people for advertising and such.
